2. It appears that upon a complaint filed by the Sub-Divisional Controller of Food, Bagerhat to the effect that the petitioner contractor took delivery of 730 maunds and 20 seers of wheat from Maheswarpara Godown for giving delivery of the same to the L.S.D., Godown at Gopalgonj, has misappropriated the entire consignment without delivery of the same to the Godown for his personal gain and that over and above this non-delivery of the wheat the accused petitioner took freight bill from the Government on production of false invoice and other connected documents and the freight bill was encased by him at Sonali Bank, Bagerhat, the Sub-Divisional Magistrate took cognizance in the matter and held a judicial enquiry by a Magistrate who after having enquired the same and having found no case against the petitioner submitted a report to the effect that the allegations against the accused petitioner have not been proved. On that the learned Sub- Divisional Magistrate dismissed the said complaint by his order dated 18.8.82. 

 4. Mr. Kbondker Mabbub Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner has urged that the proceeding pending against the petitioner before the Special Tribunal Judge need to be quashed on the grounds that the petitioner cannot be proceeded against twice under the self-same facts the first complaint having been discharged by the learned Magistrate on merits and that the cognizance taken by the Special Tribunal was without jurisdiction for the simple reason that the allegations as made constituted no offence as under section 25 of the Special Powers Act, namely hoarding and black marketing and, further, that on the joinder of the charges both schedule and non-schedule offences one trial caused an initial illegality which would cause the cognizance taken to be without lawful authority and jurisdiction. Lastly he has urged that in view of the agreement with the government by the accused petitioner, the non-delivery of goods if any, would give rise to a civil liability only and for that initiation of a criminal proceeding amounts to a sheer abuse of the process of the court and need be quashed. 

 5. There is substance in the contention of the learned Advocate and they need consideration. It appears from a clear reading of the complaint as made by the Sub- Divisional Controller of Food that the accused petitioner allegedly took delivery of certain property as a carrier and contractor employed by the Government to deliver to the Government Godown the same as required under the contract but had misappropriated the entire delivered goods namely 730 maunds and 20 seers of wheat in the process committing an offence punishable under section 407 of the Penal Code. This has nothing to do with hoarding or black marketing as there is no allegations to the effect that the petitioner had hoarded the alleged food stuff without being authorised to do so by the appropriate authority or he had sold any food stuff in black market. Hence there is no ingredients of the offence which would constitute hoarding or black marketing to attract section 25 of the Special Powers Act and if section 25 of the Special Powers Act was not attracted, cognizance taken by the Special Tribunal would be without jurisdiction. The cognizance taken further appears to suffer from an inherent initial illegality as schedule and non-schedule offences were joined altogether to be tried by the Special Tribunal at one trial which Tribunal was constituted only to try cases mentioned in the schedule of the Special Law namely the Special Powers Act and not for offences under the ordinary penal laws of the land. The joinder of schedule offences and non-schedule offences was thus illegal and the trial by the Special Tribunal of both schedule and non-schedule offences and so also the cognizance taken by the Special Tribunal of both schedule and non-schedule offences were without jurisdiction and lawful authority which need to be corrected by quashing the same. In the view we have taken here-in-before. In are supported by a decision of thiscourt reported in 33 D.L.R. at page 203.
